OPENING HOOK [speaker]. Pet owners will go to extreme lengths for their pets: Gen Z say one in five would "sell an organ" to pay for their animal.

62% of UK households own a pet: 36.5 million pets, 28.5 million of them dogs and cats. Of the 22.2 million adults in Great Britain with a pet, about 10 million (45%) are aged 16 to 40 (ONS, September 2025; 16 to 40 estimated by splitting the 30 to 49 group evenly). If asked: ONS publishes 16-29 and 30-49 only; 16-49 is exactly 13.5 million (61%).

Bridge line [speaker name]: insurers pay for late, expensive claims. If good care is visible, it can be rewarded with a lower premium. Then switch to the live site: Alex walks through the user journey (about 2 min), Paul runs the Movement check live on the Health tab (about 35 s, Pomeranian clip), then come back to the deck for the next page.

OPENING (about 10 s). Team FinPet. Our product is Petra: it makes your pet bills work for you. Then on to the problem.

PAUL. Demo on the site first (about 27 s): Health tab, "Once a week, the owner films ten seconds of their pet walking past them. That's the Movement check." Pomeranian at home, "Let's take this Pomeranian." Skeleton plays: "Our pose model finds twenty-one body points on every frame. We follow two of them: the head and the base of the tail. When a leg hurts, the body dips less on that step, so the dips stop matching." Red box: "Here the front left doesn't match, so it turns red." Click Analyse, let the result show, then switch to this slide. Why we built it (about 20 s): Every year, around two hundred thousand dogs in the UK are diagnosed with arthritis. Most are found late, because owners think the stiffness is just old age. Cats are worse: six in ten cats over six have arthritis, and most never visibly limp. This slide (about 30 s): And everything behind it is published and peer reviewed. The pose model is SuperAnimal, from EPFL, published in Nature Communications. It was trained on more than eighty-five thousand labelled animal images across forty-five species, so we didn't need anyone's pet videos to build it. The rule comes from vet gait studies that measured head and hip movement with motion capture in lame and sound dogs. Cats hide pain, so for cats we time each paw instead. (Press right arrow.) Sources: Anderson 2018 Sci Rep; Slingerland 2011 Vet J; Stadig 2016 Acta Vet Scand; Ye et al. 2024 Nat Commun; Bergh et al. 2018 Acta Vet Scand; Gómez Álvarez et al. 2017 Vet J.

PAUL, slide 9 (about 20 s): And it's built to pass regulation. Under the Veterinary Surgeons Act, only a vet can diagnose, so we screen and refer. Under UK GDPR, the video stays with the owner, and the insurer only ever sees "check done". And under the FCA's Consumer Duty, a result can only lower the price, never raise it. Nic will show you the numbers. (Press right arrow.) Sources on screen: legislation.gov.uk (Veterinary Surgeons Act 1966 s.19; UK GDPR Art. 5), FCA Handbook PRIN 2A.4.

FINANCE, Nic. Insurers pay us; owners get Petra free in their insurer's app. Two fees: £8 per active pet a year, plus 15% of verified claims savings. The Petra Pro Walk Companion is a clip-on collar wearable: when walk targets are met, the premium comes down, up to 15%. What's on the market: Napo and Tractive teamed up in December 2025. Napo customers get a free GPS tracker, but they pay the Tractive subscription, and the tracker and the policy are separate. With Petra, the wearable is part of the policy: walks on target lower the price, and the 10-second movement check catches a limp early.

Owners pay £0 for the check. Optional Petra Pro is £2.99 a month: dog cafés, groomers, food and partner discounts. That undercuts PitPat LIFE at £3.99 and DogCity at £4.99 a month.

About 12.4 million dogs, cats and rabbits in the UK are insured. At Petra's proposed £8 per pet a year, that is a pool of about £99 million a year in platform fees alone, before the 15% share of verified savings. Every 1% of insured pets we sign up is roughly £1 million a year.

Nic. The brief asked for value for all four parties, nobody at another’s expense. Here it is for one insurer with 100,000 policies, if 30% engage and their claims fall 12%.

Pet parent: up to 15% off, about £16 a year on average, up to £58, and it can never go up. Free check and walks in their insurer’s app.

Vet: about 3,000 extra online consults a year, pre-triaged with a brief and the clip. Earlier is cheaper to treat. That one is our estimate.

Insurer: about £350k a year better off after our fees and the discounts, a 1.4 times return, including £237k kept through retention. They keep 85p of every pound saved, and they win young owners: 58% of 25 to 34 year olds have a dog.

Underwriter: £965k of claims avoided, the loss ratio on engaged pets drops from about 69% to 63%, and it breaks even at just 6.9% fewer claims. They see only "check done" and the tier, never videos or health answers.

If asked about the 12%: it is our base assumption; car telematics insurers report claims 30% cheaper for young drivers, and the pilot’s control group tests it.

CLOSE (about 25 s). Why we exist: owners already do the care that prevents claims, but nobody sees it, so nobody rewards it. Petra makes it count: earlier care for the pet, lower bills for the owner, fewer claims for the insurer.

What is new: Tractive tracks, Joii and FirstVet consult, Napo hands out a tracker. Petra is the one that links the walk, the vet and the premium in one policy, inside the insurer’s own app.

Final line: lend us your expertise to help Petra follow the money, and stop insurers keeping young pet owners on a collar. Make managing your pet’s finances a walk in the park. Thank you, we would love your questions.
